stories.title: Pediatric research for the future of children: introduction to the conference proceedings
stories.description: The inaugural Pediatric Research Forum for the Future of Children (PRFC), held in Geneva, Switzerland, brought together leading investigators and emerging scientists from across the globe to discuss the future trajectory of pediatric research. Organized collaboratively by the Society for Pediatric Research (SPR) and the European Society for Paediatric Research (ESPR), the meeting was designed to foster international collaboration, highlight transformative research directions, and cultivate the next generation of pediatric clinician-scientists. A distinctive feature of the conference was its paired presentation format, in which established senior investigators presented alongside early-career researchers across five thematic domains: precision medicine and novel therapies, big data in pediatric research, early life determinants of health and disease, child mental health and development, and global pediatric research and workforce development. The meeting emphasized the importance of interdisciplinary science, equitable global partnerships, and translational pathways that accelerate the integration of discoveries into clinical practice. Key insights included the rapid expansion of genomic medicine in pediatrics, the potential and limitations of artificial intelligence and big data, the profound influence of early life exposures on lifelong health trajectories, the urgent need to address pediatric mental health, and the critical role of global collaboration and clinician-scientist training in advancing child health. The PRFC demonstrated that innovative meeting structures and cross-generational dialog can catalyze new research directions and strengthen the pediatric research ecosystem.

stories.title: Transport Minister Announces December 10 Relaunch for Somali Airlines Following International Aviation Coding
stories.description: MOGADISHU, Somalia’s Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, Mohamed Farah Nuh, has officially announced that the nation’s historic flag carrier, Somali Airlines, will return to the skies on December 10, 2026, ending an absence of more than three decades. Speaking on the planned revival, Minister Nuh assured the public that preparations are complete ahead of an inauguration ceremony scheduled for next month. International Aviation Certification and Global Recognition Confirming the new timeline, Minister Nuh stated that citizens will witness the return of the national carrier during the December 10 inauguration event. “Somali Airlines is being brought back this coming December, and its official launch will be seen,” the minister said. According to transport officials, the announcement follows the issuance and global circulation of Somali Airlines’ official International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) designator code. Under international aviation protocols, transmitting the code confirms that the carrier is legally certified to operate across international borders, ensuring that air traffic controllers, radar networks, and foreign airports officially recognize and accept Somali Airlines flights. A History of Repeatedly Postponed Timelines Originally founded in 1964, Somali Airlines once connected Mogadishu to regional hubs such as Nairobi and Dar es Salaam alongside European and Middle Eastern destinations including Rome and Frankfurt, before suspending operations in January 1991 following the collapse of the central government and the outbreak of civil war. Efforts to revive the state-owned carrier have faced repeated delays over the past several years. After the Civil Aviation Minister vowed to revive Somali Airlines upon assuming office, federal authorities announced in July 2025 that Somalia acquired two Airbus planes to re-establish its fleet. Earlier this year, the government set a September deadline for the flag carrier’s resumption, a target that passed without commercial passenger flights taking off. stories.title: Expression of GPX4 and redox balance are critical for intestinal intraepithelial lymphocytes homeostasis
stories.description: Intestinal intraepithelial lymphocytes (IELs) provide frontline mucosal defense while functioning within a hypoxic epithelial niche characterized by sustained oxidative stress. Their distinctive mitochondrial and metabolic features may predispose them to oxidative damage; however, how IELs maintain viability under these conditions remains unclear. Here we showed that IELs engaged robust antioxidant transcriptional programs and identified glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) as a cell-intrinsic factor selectively required for IEL maintenance. Conditional deletion of Gpx4 in CD8+ T cells or TCRαβ+ T cells caused profound loss of IELs, without affecting peripheral T cell compartments. Gpx4-deficient IELs accumulated reactive oxygen species, underwent lipid peroxidation and succumbed to ferroptotic cell death, a phenotype rescued by vitamin E supplementation. Functionally, loss of Gpx4 increased susceptibility to enteric infection in mice, while reduced GPX4 expression was associated with pathology of inflammatory bowel disease in humans, establishing GPX4-dependent control of ferroptosis as a central mechanism sustaining IEL survival and intestinal barrier immunity. Colonna and colleagues show that cell-intrinsic expression of GPX4 is required for intestinal intraepithelial lymphocytes homeostasis.

stories.title: A TNF-producing neutrophil subset drives age-dependent hepatotoxicity in mice
stories.description: The mechanisms by which aging contributes to the detrimental effect of cancer therapy are unclear. Here we show that while a synthetic double-stranded RNA (poly-inosinic:cytidylic acid (polyIC)) suppresses liver tumors in young mice, it induces lethal liver damage in aged mice. Single-cell and functional analyses show a CD14+ neutrophil subset that has robust TNF induction by polyIC in the aged liver. Impaired expression of nuclear receptors (including NR3C1) and elevated NF-κB and AP-1 signaling drive a skewing toward Tnf+ over Saa1+ neutrophils in the aged liver. TNF neutralization rescued polyIC-induced mortality, while enhancing its anti-tumor effect in aged mice. Expression of TNF+SAA1− neutrophil signature genes is associated with reduced survival in patients with liver cancer aged >60 years. This study identifies a detrimental mechanism in the aged liver, which is undetectable under basal conditions. We also provide a strategy to improve therapeutic outcomes in older patients by mitigating treatment-associated toxicity. Cancer immunotherapies generally do not work as well and are more prone to adverse effects in older patients. Here the authors show a skewing of liver neutrophils from a Saa1+ population to a population with higher levels of TNF production in aging mice that might explain some age-related differences in the therapeutic response to liver cancer.

stories.title: Complete biosynthesis and production of paclitaxel in a plant host
stories.description: Paclitaxel (Taxol) is a cornerstone chemotherapeutic agent, but its structural complexity and low natural abundance make its production costly and inefficient. Although several partial and divergent biosynthetic schemes have been proposed, the complete pathway has not been fully validated. Here we report the full reconstruction of the paclitaxel biosynthetic pathway in Nicotiana benthamiana, systematically resolving outstanding mechanistic uncertainties. We validate enzyme functions through isolation and nuclear magnetic resonance-based structural characterization of key pathway intermediates and refine the order of catalytic steps. We further show that critical biosynthetic steps are compartmentalized across multiple organelles, requiring directional relocations of intermediates among plastids, the endoplasmic reticulum, cytosol and peroxisomes. Guided by these insights, we implement targeted engineering strategies that increase paclitaxel accumulation by more than 500-fold, reaching 61.05 µg g−1 dry weight, comparable to levels in Taxus bark. This work establishes a chemically validated and functionally reconstructed paclitaxel biosynthetic pathway and provides proof of concept for its biotechnological production in plants. Paclitaxel is an important but costly anticancer drug whose complex biosynthesis has remained partially undiscovered. Here Liang et al. reconstruct and chemically validate its complete pathway in a model plant, uncover essential trafficking between cell compartments and raise its production levels in tobacco.

stories.title: Geometry-driven polarization control in ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals
stories.description: Ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals (FNLCs) combine fluidity with spontaneous polarization, offering promising avenues for flexible electromechanical systems. Here, we demonstrate that mechano-electrical conversion in FNLCs can be enhanced by mechanically programming a robust macroscopic polarization alignment. Using hybrid liquid crystal cells composed of a rigid glass substrate and a flexible substrate, with no alignment treatment on either surface, we show that mechanically deforming the cell in the ferroelectric nematic phase suppresses polarization domains and produces long-range polarization alignment over millimeter-scale areas. Importantly, geometry-driven polarization selection remains effective in a 180-μm-thick cell, demonstrating macroscopic polarization control without surface alignment treatment even in a thickness regime where surface-controlled monodomain alignment is difficult. This geometry-driven alignment is attributed to coupling between the deformation-imposed cell geometry and a preferred splay tendency of the polar phase, and we further find that the selected polarization direction exhibits clear material dependence. Leveraging this deformation-enabled alignment, we develop a proof-of-concept FNLC-based energy harvester that converts mechanical deformation into an output of approximately 1 V. These findings establish geometry-driven alignment as a practical design strategy for boosting FNLC mechano-electrical conversion while providing polarization control for soft electronic devices.
